secondary.note: As predicted by explore-agent's crawl-log, client-visible XHR/fetch capture across all 8 page folders is sparse because this Next.js frontend fetches almost everything server-side via RSC. The only client-visible API call observed in ANY capture is GET https://api.eventhub.rahulshettyacademy.com/api/config (seen in home/ and login/ captures), which matches GET /config in the Swagger spec exactly -- this cross-reference confirms the Swagger spec is live/accurate for at least this endpoint. Also of note: all 8 captures independently observed intermittent 503s on Next.js RSC prefetches (_rsc= query requests) for /events/283, /events/284, /events/285 when prefetched from the /events listing or home page -- this is a frontend RSC/SSR reliability signal, not a documented REST endpoint, so it is not in the endpoint table below but IS carried into the test plan's reliability/negative section per the clarifications doc.

contractDiscrepancyFlag.issue: Swagger spec declares `security: [{bearerAuth: []}]` ONLY on GET /auth/me. GET/POST /bookings, GET/PUT/DELETE /bookings/:id, GET /bookings/ref/:ref, and all /events endpoints are documented with no security requirement at all. However info.description states 'Each registered user gets a fully isolated sandbox -- events and bookings are private to their account,' which implies bookings (and possibly events) ARE user-scoped and should require a bearer token in practice.
contractDiscrepancyFlag.impact: This is either (a) a spec-documentation bug where @ApiBearerAuth()/security annotations were omitted on most controllers, or (b) these routes are genuinely unauthenticated globally-shared data despite the per-account-sandbox description. Both are plausible for a scaffolded/demo NestJS+Swagger app.
contractDiscrepancyFlag.testPlanTreatment: Encoded as an explicit Auth/contract test case per affected endpoint: call with a valid token, with no Authorization header, and with an invalid/malformed token, and assert whatever the live API actually does (200 vs 401) is treated as the ground truth going forward -- the spec's silence on `security` is not assumed to mean 'no auth enforced.'

unbackedFrontendFeatures.finding: No bulk/batch-delete endpoint (e.g. `DELETE /api/bookings`, `POST /api/bookings/clear-all`) exists anywhere in the live OpenAPI spec (re-confirmed this run -- same 10 paths as before). The only deletion primitive documented for bookings is the singular `DELETE /api/bookings/{id}`. Most likely implementation: the frontend fetches the account's full booking list client-side then issues one `DELETE /api/bookings/{id}` call per booking in a loop, OR a server route exists that was simply never annotated/surfaced in the Swagger doc (undocumented route -- cannot be ruled out from static discovery alone). Documented as a functional/negative/boundary scenario set in api-test-plan.md; not called by any generated test regardless of which theory is correct, per this run's non-mutation authorization.

No dedicated eviction endpoint exists. Per the admin page's own banner copy ('You can add up to 6 events. Once the limit is reached, your oldest event is automatically replaced when you add a new one.' -- artifacts/eventhub/explore/pages/admin/dom-snapshot.md), this is almost certainly server-side business logic embedded inside the existing `POST /api/events` handler itself (i.e. a 7th `POST /events` call, while the account already owns 6, triggers an automatic server-side deletion of the oldest owned event as a side effect of that same request) rather than a separate route being called by the frontend. Documented as a boundary scenario on `POST /api/events` in api-test-plan.md; not executed live (orchestrator explicitly declined to authorize live execution of this flow -- see clarifications doc's 'Orchestrator-level non-execution override').

appWideRunExtension.rbacFinding: No role/permission field is exposed anywhere in the documented API surface -- `GET /auth/me`'s MeResponse schema only returns `{userId, email}`, no `role`/`isAdmin`/`permissions` claim. `POST /events`, `PUT /events/{id}`, and `DELETE /events/{id}` (the admin-mutation routes) declare no `security` requirement at all in the spec, the same contract-discrepancy pattern already flagged above for Bookings. This means either (a) admin-gating for /admin/events is enforced purely at the Next.js frontend/UI layer with zero backend authorization check on the mutating Events routes, or (b) a server-side role check exists but simply isn't reflected in the Swagger annotations. This is the single most significant open question surfaced by this run for a future authorization-bypass follow-up (e.g. calling `POST /events` with a non-admin token, an expired token, or no token at all, and confirming whether it's rejected). Not executed live in this run -- calling any Events-mutation route is out of scope per this run's GET-only authorization regardless of the credential used -- but written into api-test-plan.md's RBAC section as the specific empirical question a human/future authorized run should resolve next.
appWideRunExtension.passwordPolicyDiscrepancy: The frontend /register form displays and (per the UI suite's live-verified testing) enforces a strict client-side password policy: >= 8 characters, 1 uppercase letter, 1 number, 1 special character. The backend's documented `AuthInput` schema (used by both `POST /auth/register` and `POST /auth/login`) declares only `password: { type: string, minLength: 6 }` -- no complexity requirements at all. This is a genuine contract gap: a password satisfying the backend's documented minimum (e.g. 'abcdef', 6 lowercase letters, no number/symbol) would be rejected by the frontend's client-side validation before ever reaching the network, but nothing in the documented API contract itself would stop such a password from being accepted if `POST /auth/register` were called directly (bypassing the UI). Not verified live (POST /auth/register is not executed in this run per its non-mutation authorization) -- flagged as a contract question for a future authorized run: does the *backend* also enforce the complexity policy server-side, or does it rely entirely on the frontend?
appWideRunExtension.cityFilterDataAnomaly: Seeded event id=284 ('Hollywood Monsoon Night -- Los Angeles') has `city: "Los Angeles"`, a value NOT present in the frontend's City filter dropdown's 6 fixed options (Mumbai, Bangalore, Delhi, Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune), per the clarifications doc. This is scoped as a UI dropdown/seed-data mismatch, not a documented API defect: the `city` query param on `GET /events` has no `enum` constraint in the spec (unlike `category`, which does), so the API itself is expected to accept and correctly filter on an arbitrary city string including 'Los Angeles'. Tested at the API level in events-search-filter.spec.ts: `GET /api/events?city=Los%20Angeles` is expected to still return event 284 correctly, which would confirm the gap is purely in the frontend's fixed dropdown option list, not in the API's filtering capability.
